title: Long gameplay recordings become searchable scene blocks
summary: YTIntel now turns long private gameplay uploads into a searchable Scene Index. After an uploaded video is banked, the browser can automatically sample it, detect strong visual boundaries, build practical 10–75 second virtual clips, create private scene thumbnails, optionally enrich representative frames with on-device vision, and rank the resulting scenes against a commentary script or the current Analyse. The original source recording stays untouched, avoiding hours of wasteful browser re-encoding.
discord_changes: 🎬 AUTOMATIC SCENE INDEX: long Creator Assets recordings can now become practical 10–75 second searchable virtual clips after upload.
🖼️ PRIVATE THUMBNAILS + TAGS: YTIntel samples the recording, detects strong visual changes, banks private scene thumbnails and adds deterministic visual/search tags.

🧠 OPTIONAL LOCAL VISION: when YTIntel's on-device vision model is already available, representative scenes are enriched with production mode, composition, visible text, narrative role and attention-device labels.
🔎 SCRIPT → B-ROLL SEARCH: paste a commentary script or use the current Analyse and YTIntel ranks the most relevant indexed gameplay scenes with exact start/end timestamps and copyable clip recipes.
changes: Added v377-scene-indexer.js and a new Scene index workspace inside Creator Assets in Vault.
Added a private ytintel_creator_scenes Supabase table with authenticated per-user RLS, asset foreign keys, exact timestamps, visual metadata, search text, tags and private thumbnail paths.
Applied an adaptive RGB-histogram scene-boundary detector in the browser with up to 480 samples per source recording, 10-second minimum scene blocks and 75-second maximum practical background blocks.

Scene indexing creates virtual clips instead of immediately transcoding the original recording. This preserves the full-quality source and stores exact start/end recipes for later trimming only when a clip is actually needed.
Added private scene-thumbnail capture and upload. Each scene row can store representative time, change score, brightness, motion hint, thumbnail path and search metadata.

When local multimodal AI is already enabled, YTIntel can enrich a spread of representative scenes with production mode, composition, visible text, narrative role, attention devices and confidence without paid API credits.
Added commentary-script footage search with query-term extraction, concept expansion and ranking across source metadata, scene tags and local-vision labels.
Added a Use current Analyse action that turns the current winner analysis context into a Creator Assets scene search, closing the loop from research → remake → matching B-roll.
Added Preview source and Copy clip recipe actions so every search result carries an exact source title, start, end, duration and scene tags.
Added automatic post-upload handoff for newly banked video files plus manual Index scenes / Re-index scenes controls for existing cloud recordings.
Added a dedicated v0.37.7 schema/contract test and upgraded CI, Pages validation, PWA cache/versioning and production browser expectations.
known_limitations: Scene blocks are virtual timestamp ranges, not physically transcoded standalone video files yet. This is intentional for speed and source-quality preservation; a later trim/export stage can materialise only selected clips.
Scene detection is sampled rather than frame-by-frame. Long recordings are capped at 480 sample points, so extremely brief cuts between samples may not become separate scene blocks.
Deterministic tags are intentionally conservative. Rich semantic scene labels are strongest when the optional on-device vision model is already available in a compatible browser.

The first automatic indexing pass runs in the browser. Closing the tab or putting a mobile browser to sleep can interrupt indexing; the original uploaded recording remains safely banked and can be re-indexed later.

Private thumbnails are stored separately from the original recording. Re-indexing removes known prior scene rows and attempts to clean their known thumbnail files, but an interrupted cleanup can leave harmless orphaned thumbnail objects.
Actual upload capacity remains governed by the Supabase project's global and bucket Storage limits.
Creator-facing physical clip delivery, transcoding/proxy generation, waveform-derived audio tagging, embeddings/vector search and CDN distribution remain future Endgame milestones.
Publisher/platform rights still govern gameplay redistribution. YTIntel does not treat self-recording as automatic permission to sublicense gameplay footage.
why_it_matters: The Creator Assets moat becomes useful only when hours of raw gameplay can turn into the exact B-roll a creator needs without manually scrubbing every recording. v0.37.7 establishes that retrieval layer: upload once, index into timestamped visual scene blocks, then search those blocks from the script or video plan you are actually making.
